notes: The text says Nano Every, but the circuit image, pin labels and Arduino Editor screenshot show Arduino Nano 33 BLE boards, so the arduino-nano-33-ble catalogue type is used.

The circuit image draws wires directly between pins and resistors with no breadboard. The manual's parts list includes mini breadboards, so I used one breadboard (bb1) as the junction for the two pull-up resistors and the shared SDA/SCL/3V/GND nets. Wires are male-to-female jumpers: female end on the board pin, male end in the breadboard.

The image shows reader A5 wired to writer A5 (SCL) and reader A4 to writer A4 (SDA). Each line has a 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3V. The 3V comes only from the reader board's 3V pin. The writer's 3V pin is not connected.
The manual lists 10 jumper wires and 2 mini breadboards, but the circuit needs only 7 wires and one breadboard. Resistor positions on the breadboard are chosen arbitrarily.
Both boards are connected to the computer by USB. The computer is not modelled as a part. The writer's USB is required for the Serial Monitor. The reader needs power only.
